$comment: ROADMAP Phase 1A step 10 - deterministic simulation logging and replay evidence. schemas/fight_event.schema.json already defines what an event LOOKS like; nothing until now defined what the log GUARANTEES. Two distinct contracts live here and are deliberately not merged: resimulation (same seed and initial state reproduce the same authoritative event log) and replay (a saved log reproduces the recorded presentation without re-running uncertain decisions). Conflating them is how a replay system starts silently re-deciding fights. Engine-neutral definitions only (Rule 18). Semantics: docs/phase1a/logging_and_replay.md.

resimulation.$comment: Decision 0002 / Criterion E.19. Validated in-engine at four levels already (determinism_probe_results.md Phases A-E); this is the contract those probes were testing against.
resimulation.notes: Anything excluded from the hash is also forbidden from writing simulation state - the camera model already declares exactly that, which is what makes the exclusion safe rather than convenient.

replay.$comment: Rule 13 and Rule 3. A replay re-presents; it never re-decides.
replay.notes: Camera is the one thing a replay may choose freely, because the camera writes no simulation state. Everything else is read from the log as recorded.

log_requirements.notes: The ROADMAP gate asks that the log explain major combat and judging events. 'Explained' means the event names the earlier seq values it causally follows, so a reader can walk backwards from a stoppage to the exchange that caused it.

prohibitions: Re-run CPU decisions, judging or the RNG during replay (Rule 13).
Let wall-clock time, frame rate or container ordering affect the authoritative log (Criterion E.19).
Include camera or presentation state in the determinism hash.
Emit a sealed judge event as observable, or reveal one before the archival reveal (Rule 3).
Write an explains reference to a later sequence number.
Record a major combat or judging event with no causal explanation (ROADMAP gate).

invariants.statement: Same seed, same authoritative initial state and same authored data reproduce a byte-identical authoritative event log.
Camera and presentation are excluded from the determinism hash, and every excluded system is one that writes no simulation state.
Replay re-runs neither CPU decisions, nor judging, nor the RNG; it re-presents a recorded log.
Sealed judge events are visible only at the archival reveal, never during the fight or the immediate result flow, and replay does not widen that.
Sequence and tick are monotonic and every event carries the authoritative clock.
An explains reference names an earlier sequence number; nothing is caused by its own future.
Punch outcomes, knockdowns, stoppages, deductions and both judge cards must carry causal explanation, so a reader can walk backwards from a result to the exchange that produced it.
Every type named here exists in fight_event.schema.json, and every sealed type named by the score-isolation contract is marked sealed here.
